target_customer: People trying to quit alcohol, nicotine or other substances, with Medicaid and cash-pay clinic services as the planned payer base
problem: Addiction treatment has long waitlists for therapy and medication; people lack daily support between treatments.
business_model: Consumer subscription app plus telemedicine clinic (intake fee of $20 and $89 per month for medication, per the clinic site)
product_category: Sobriety app and AI-native telemedicine addiction clinic

founders.name: Koby Conrad
prior_employers: Rupa (led Growth from $5M to $75M per year, per YC page)
previous_startups: YC S19 company, unnamed on the YC page
founders.background_notes: Growth marketer and angel investor per YC page; a podcast page says he taught himself to code and wrote the book Channels of Growth.

competitors.name: Soberly
competitors.what: Sobriety tracker with AI recovery companion

competitors.name: SoberAI / AA Sponsor
competitors.what: AI sponsor personalities, subscription $89 per year

technical_complexity.rationale: A consumer app with an AI chat sponsor is standard engineering; the clinical telemedicine layer adds licensing and compliance work rather than research-grade technology.

defensibility.rationale: The AI sponsor is copyable and many sobriety apps exist. Licensed clinicians and a streak-based habit add some switching costs.

market_need_then: Large addiction treatment waitlists and heavy Medicaid spending on substance use treatment. The company states over 18,750 waitlisted patients and about $1.5M run-rate subscription revenue, company-reported only.

branding.domain_note: App domain sunflowersober.com and clinic domain sunflowerclinic.com rather than sunflower.com.

identity.visual_style: Warm, painted landscapes, sunflower fields, yellow, blue and green accents
identity.voice_and_tone: Warm and supportive; mission to create one trillion days of sobriety

branding.brand_signature: Users earn a sunflower for each sober day
branding.community_and_virality: App includes a community and free weekly peer support groups; the company claims one of the largest brands in sobriety, unverified.

brand_strength.rationale: A clear sunflower mechanic and warm identity tied to the product, but the evidence of brand pull is company-reported only.

outcome_analysis: The company is active with no exit. It grew a consumer sobriety app on a growth-marketing founder's skills, raised a seed in late 2025 according to aggregators, and is now adding clinical services. Success depends on converting app users to paid clinic care.
notes: Funding conflicts. The clinic site claims over $9.5M raised from Y Combinator, a16z speedrun, Flybridge, Rebel Fund and Alumni Ventures. Wellfound shows a $6.2M seed (November 2025) and a $1.3M pre-seed, and a Seedtable or Standout page shows $6.5M total at a $60M post-money from a founder post. A 2024 press release cited a $350,000 pre-seed. Round investors list is from the company site and may span rounds. Some aggregators label the company YC Fall 2025 while the YC page says Summer 2026. Founded 2024 per YC page; the app itself existed earlier under the developer name. Competition is dated from the company founding year only as far as sources allow. No outcome news found.
